Route 9 checked anyway: raw .sav counts reversed per the .do equal live item x resp counts in 8/8 cells (resp1..4: ids04 2230/8280/16102/1275; ids12 705/3240/20313/2421). Ns/Nc (ids04 1416, ids12 2624) is absent from the table; no system-missing in the .sav for these columns (both questions are asked of everyone; the skip instructions after questions 8-10 route to question 12); 28754 of 29303 records appear, 54566 rows. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the question stems verbatim; both end in an ellipsis with no question mark because the read-out options complete the question (…muy buena? etc.), and are shipped that way. option_text = the questionnaire / documentation option wording (…muy buena? … …muy mala? for question 4, masculine …muy bueno? … …muy malo? for question 12). Deviation: the .sav value labels read '. …muy buena?' with a leading '. ' left over from the printed numbering (1. …muy buena?); that artifact is stripped. SECTIONS: two section_ids, one per item, because the two questions sit under different read-aloud legends (asterisked text, which the questionnaire's format conventions define as read by the interviewer): section _1 (ids04) = the legend above DS question 3 (*A partir de ahora le haré algunas preguntas sobre la [Policía Provincial/Policía de la Ciudad]*), which opens the block containing question 4; section _2 (ids12) = the legend above DS question 7 (*Recuerde que estas preguntas se refieren únicamente a la [Policía Provincial/Policía de la Ciudad]*), which opens the block containing question 12. They are kept because they supply the referent of la policía; the bracket is the interviewer's fill, kept as the questionnaire's own placeholder; asterisks dropped, line wraps joined. The same Recuerde legend is also printed above question 13 (fairness, batch_594, where it went in instructions because that table is one question). instructions blank: no text applies identically to both items. Not shipped: the chapter legend introducing DS question 1. language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation: INDEC publishes the ENV 2017 in Spanish only; English in the _translated columns produced by IRW (both genders of the options render as …very good? etc.).
